Sprint 0 – Problem Framing, Infrastructure Setup & RAG Foundations

Hands-On Section
Lesson 7
Video 1: I
n the following video we explore the Amazon Items Dataset.
Video 2 (Notebook): I
n the following video we:
Preprocess Amazon items dataset and make it ready for writing to Qdrant.
Spin up a local Qdrant database.
Write the Amazon items dataset to the Qdrant DB.
Video 3 (Notebook):
In the following video we implement a simple RAG pipeline:
User query is passed to the embedding model to produce a vector representation of the query.
The embedding vector is used to perform ANN search using Cosine similarity to retrieve text chunks closest to the query in the vector space.
Retrieved context, together with the user query is rendered into a prompt.
The prompt is passed to an LLM to produce the final answer which is returned to the user via the streamlit application.
Video 4 (Backend + Frontend):
In the following video we move the RAG pipeline logic to our Backend application and adjust our Frontend application to be able to communicate wit the backend given the changes.
Video 5 (Backend):
In the following video we implement basic observability foundations for our RAG pipeline.
Video 6 (Notebook):
In the following video we create a synthetic dataset that will be used for initial RAG pipeline evaluation.
Video 7 (Notebook):
In the following video we test out RAGAS framework to run evals on one of the examples stored in LangSmith dataset.
Video 8 (Backend):
In the following video we move our RAGAS evals into a separate script that is able to calculate the metrics agains the entire LangSmith dataset and store the results within the platform.

Sprint 4 – Multi-Agent Systems
📄
Hands-on Section
Lesson 5
Video 1 (Notebook):
In the following video we lay ground for a new agent in our system that would be capable to manage the user's shopping cart. We create the shopping cart tables in our postgres database and implement three functions (tools) to manipulate data in the table:
Add to shopping cart.
Get the data of the shopping cart.
Remove item from the shopping cart.
Video 2 (Notebook):
In the following video we implement a new agent (Shopping Cart Agent) that is given tools from the previous video and is able to perform shopping cart operations accordingly. We also connect this agent to our Graph and adjust the router node with additional user intent - shopping cart operations.
Video 3 (Backend):
In the following video I implement a Coordinator Agent that:
Plans the multistep workflow to answer the users query.
Routes user intent to either Product Q&A Agent or the Shopping Cart Agent.
Gets the control of the system back once the Worker Agents complete their work and adjust the plan according to the final system state.
Video 4 (Backend):
In the following video we move the Coordinator and Shopping Cart Agents as well as Graph adjustments to our backend and implement a new capability that allows our frontend to display the lates state of the user's shopping cart. With this capability we can explore the potential of the agent in a more convenient way. Every time we attempt some cart manipulation via the chatbot, we will see the adjustments made to our cart in real time in the UI:
Video 5 (Notebook):
In the following video we lay the foundations for a new Warehouse Manager Agent:
We create a table in the Postgres database to support the functionality.
We then populate it with synthetic data about items that are present in our Qdrant collection.
Video 6 (Notebook):
In the following video I implement tools that will be used by the Warehouse Manager Agent:
Video 7 (Notebook):
In the following video we implement the Warehouse Manager Agent to be part of our LangGraph Graph:
Video 8 (Backend):
In the following video we move the previously implemented agent to our backend codebase.
